candidate.answerReason: Rewriting every base as a power of 10 gives 10^(5x)=10^15, which has the unique real solution x=3.

methods.label: Express every power with base 10
methods.explanation:
The bases \(100\) and \(1000\) are powers of \(10\), so using a common base lets us compare the exponents. For real \(x\), the positive-base power laws give
\[
10^x\cdot100^{2x}
=10^x\cdot(10^2)^{2x}
=10^{x+4x}=10^{5x}.
\]
Also, \(1000^5=(10^3)^5=10^{15}\). Thus the equation becomes \(10^{5x}=10^{15}\).

Since powers of \(10\) increase strictly as their real exponents increase, equal powers must have equal exponents. Therefore \(5x=15\), so \(\boxed{x=3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
